findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

The plan is mostly complete and coherent. It opens with a mental model and a risk-first proving slice, and it covers all 12 scenario blocks with real-boundary proofs. Its decisions are traceable: the four records name alternatives and why they lost, the evidence records are current, the durable architecture record resolves, Data applicability has a decision for every subject, Measurement applicability is a reasoned skip, and the trust boundaries are honest. The independent 37-case map enumerates exactly 37 cases. Each cited assertion name corresponds to a real test title in the supplied source files.  One blocking error remains. The fixed lane includes packages/cli/tests/codex-plugin-version.test.ts, and several of its tests need the external `codex` CLI. The plan never decides whether that tool is part of the execution environment. Its stated policy is no provider executables, a minimal environment, and binding only Node, Bun, Git and the launcher. Under that policy, either the codex-dependent tests fail and every observation refuses, so the demo scenario can never succeed, or an unbound tool decides the outcome. That would violate R1/R4 input binding.  Four warnings do not block: - The assertion map leaves out an available assertion for the "no plan is sent" step. - The plan does not say whether a mismatched assertion-source digest refuses at admission or is only kept on record. - The pre-execution refusal for a changed accepted scope has no explicit public-CLI proof row. - The fresh-review status of the 17-case scenario baseline is recorded in two places that are easy to misread together.  Focused reviewability: pass. Decisions stay in the main path; the investigation ledger and the assertion map are explicitly marked subordinate.

The plan leaves the fixed lane's tool inventory undecided, and the gap blocks the core success claim.  **The conflict.** The fixed lane runs packages/cli/tests/codex-plugin-version.test.ts in full. Three tests in that file spawn the external `codex` CLI and assert that it is present (`expect(marketplaceAdd.error, 'Codex CLI is required for plugin install tests').toBeUndefined()`): - 'executes from the cache path reported by a real Codex plugin install' - 'accepts a cachebusted bundle identity without repair guidance' - 'rejects a packed plugin…' (via its pack helpers)  The plan contradicts that dependency in three places: - Committed execution identity says "No provider executables… is selected" and allows "only trusted pinned/system tool paths" in a minimal environment. - Current verification re-resolves and binds only the Node, Bun, Git and launcher executables. - Success requires no unexpected failed result, and the plan says unrelated failures refuse rather than being credited.  **Consequences.** Two reasonable implementations behave in materially different ways: - (a) The codex binary is excluded. Those tests fail on every run, so the 'Complete proof produces verifiable evidence' demo scenario and the retry-success scenario can never pass. - (b) The codex binary is inherited from PATH. An unbound, provider-owned executable then decides whether observation succeeds, and replacing it does not stale current success. That violates R1/R4 ("a bound input change… prevents a successful observation"; changed execution inputs must refuse current success).  **Decision owner.** The agent, in Implementation Planning. The plan must decide which of these holds and state the consequences: - the codex CLI is a bound execution input, with path, version and digest recorded and re-verified, plus an explicit exception to the no-provider-executable rule and a statement that no network or model call occurs; - the lane's file set or the definition of required versus unrelated results…

The assertion map omits a test that already proves one of its expanded steps.  In the map's 'Corrupt reviewer copies refuse and the canonical pair dispatches' block, rows 1 and 2 expand to "no plan is sent and the phase and reconciliation action are named". Their required assertions are 'blocks … through the installed CLI with the failed copy named' and 'names the phase and repair action for …'. Neither asserts non-dispatch. The supplied file contains 'Execution Plan review-contract identity refuses stale-reviewer before dispatching its plan to a reviewer' (and the stale-slicing-contract variant), which asserts `reviewerDispatched === false`.  The observer disclaims semantic certification, but this map is presented as decision-bearing and reviewed now. Add those assertions, or record why the "no plan is sent" clause is left unmapped.

The plan does not say what happens when a test file changes after the map was authored.  The Fixed assertion contract says "Every source digest is retained", and the map records SHA-256 values for the ten assertion-source files at f211c4c30. The plan never states whether a mismatch at observation time: - refuses before execution as an unsupported or changed contract, or - is only recorded for later semantic review.  Under the second reading, a test body can be weakened while its name stays the same, and observation still succeeds. The plan disclaims semantic adequacy, so this is not a requirement violation, but the choice is load-bearing for later certification consumers. State it explicitly, with the recovery action for each outcome.

The pre-execution refusal for a changed accepted scope has no explicit public-CLI proof.  This carries over the scenario-review warning on R1: when accepted scope has changed before a run, the CLI must refuse and ask for review of an updated shipped contract. Commit-or-clean is the wrong recovery here.  The Persona consequences section states that recovery message. In the proof table, however, the 'Dirty execution configuration' row covers only dirty, untracked and ignored inputs, and the 'Meaningful changes stale' row covers scope changes only at verification time.  Add this path to an integration row or to the source-identity matrix at the real CLI entry point. Otherwise an implementation that tells the maintainer to commit or clean would pass every listed proof.

The plan's state record mixes historical and current review receipts in a way that is easy to misread.  Current and target truth cites formal scenario review 79aecfba as approving the restored 12 blocks / 17 cases. The ticket Work Log also cites bd278232 and feab7722 for earlier 17-case revisions, which are invalidated history.  The plan already separates these states correctly. One line naming 79aecfba as the only current scenario receipt, with the others as invalidated history, would help a reader avoid treating an older approval as current.

Strengths confirmed during review: - **Map completeness:** the map has exactly 37 cases (1+4+1+3+2+2+1+6+6+3+3+3+1+1). Every cited name resolves to an it/it.each title in the supplied files, including parameterized titles and both route declaration orders. - **Architecture link:** the anchor resolves to a Proposed ARCHITECTURE.md record that matches the plan. - **Data decisions:** all eleven data subjects carry decisions, the store owners agree with the stated source of truth, and Measurement applicability is a reasoned skip. - **Plan-state labels:** proposed, implemented, proven and pending-authority states are labeled separately.
